benchmark_liu_dao.name: Calligraphy 六島.svg
benchmark_liu_dao.author: Tc262
benchmark_liu_dao.note: Comparison of executional restraint, ink masses, brush gesture and whitespace only, not a character-for-character mapping; two different strings.

B_advantages: Outer enclosure has distinctive uneven movement and high visual energy
Original brush bitmap has nuanced ink texture
B_defects: Simplified Chinese 风 inner 乂 structure is obscured by many overlapping parallel sweeps
Outer right hook is visually dominant
The traced Figma vector discards important ink granularity and compresses many strokes into one path
benchmark_strengths: More controlled hierarchy between heavy brush masses and fine flicks
Distinctive spatial pauses and more legible intentional mark structures

one_new_image_attempt.actual_output: New complete black calligraphy glyph was regenerated, changing simplified 风 into traditional 風 and not preserving original B outer frame.

isolated_figma_repair.goal: Single scoped local trial — keep B outside contour, white-mask only incorrect crowded interior, insert two editable crossed strokes to express inner 乂.
isolated_figma_repair.implementation: Single new Figma page with original B and one trial B1, without mutating B parent document. A white vector mask covered inner overlapping strokes, two original vector crosses were added. Subsequent screenshot and three text annotations identify visual FAIL.
isolated_figma_repair.visual_result: B1's new inner X more closely matches correct simplified 风 shape, but is markedly smoother and mechanically geometric, inconsistent with surrounding dry-brush B outline. A few abrupt mask edges/stray black remnants remained. Fails professional design gain.
isolated_figma_repair.rollback_policy: Original B kept, candidate B1 isolated and explicitly labeled failed.

overall.authoritative_baseline: Original B is only partially positive; not final.
overall.no_promotion: B1 and invalid 風 generation not usable as approved style data.
overall.next: Stop this one-change experiment; avoid repeating geometric or prompt-only glyph edits. The next genuinely distinct investigation would need evidence-based real artist stroke sources or a structured drawing process, and an independent legibility/taste check before constructing four-character lettering.
